description: The catalog check of the decision profile v1alpha1 (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 6.9) and its place among the reasons (section 6.6). Each case is one call of a tool or a model by agent_id, whose bundle holds the catalog file catalog (section 7.7) and the policies, those of the case when it gives them, otherwise the file's: wt-catalog, the global policy that section 6.9 seeds. A case without_catalog has a bundle without a catalog file, which reads as an empty catalog. blocks are the active blocks (section 5.10): each covers the string covers, which the block carries as covered_sha256, its SHA-256; a block of a kind that section 5.10 does not name covers every tool and every model, wherever row 1 applies (EP-10, EP-15, the review of 2026-11-16). tooling is the tool or the model as the agent has it, as tooling.json writes an entry: the enforcement point computes its reference, an MCP tool's server's, and a model's endpoint, normalized, with the catalog's redaction rules (sections 4.10 and 5.10). definition is the hash of the tool's definition as the agent has it now, absent when it has none; digest is the model's digest as the runtime reports it, absent when it reports none; arguments, or arguments_text, are a tool call's arguments, absent when it has none; origin and approval are an exposure's (section 6.10). The decision comes, in this order, from the gate, whose state a case gives when it closes it; error.unknown_agent, for the case's subject when it gives one; the catalog check, rows 1 to 6 for tool.invoke, tool.expose and model.invoke, and row 1 alone for tool.result and model.result; EP-19's record of a tool call's arguments (error.invalid_request); then the policies, on the request whose resource is the catalog's entry, by its key and with its properties (section 6.3), and whose context carries the time, the record, calls_decided and digest. The expected decision names the resource by resource_id once the catalog check ran: the entry's key or, for tooling that the catalog does not list, its name as the agent sees it, with reference_sha256, the SHA-256 of its reference, absent when it makes none (EP-16, section 8.3). block_ids lists every block that covers the call, and a catalog.blocked decision names any one of them (EP-16). A response with a catalog.* reason carries bundle_version and no determining policies (section 6.6).

cases.description: A server block covers a tool of the server that the catalog lists, named by its key
A server block covers a tool of the server that the catalog does not list, named by its name with the SHA-256 of its reference
A tool block covers one of the agent's own tools, by its name
A server block and a tool block both cover the call: the decision names either
Blocks of another server and of another tool cover nothing of the call
A tool block covers a built-in tool, by its provider and its type
A provider block covers models only: the provider's built-in tool passes
A model block covers the model, by its reference
A provider block covers every model of the provider
A provider block covers a model that the catalog does not list, named by its name with the SHA-256 of its reference
An endpoint block covers every model of the endpoint
An endpoint block covers the endpoint as the model's reference writes it, normalized and then redacted with the deployment's rules
An endpoint block of the endpoint as the agent writes it, before redaction, covers nothing
Blocks cover by their kind: a tool block of the model's reference, and a model block of a tool's, cover nothing
A block of a kind that the enforcement point does not know covers every tool: tool.invoke
A block of an unknown kind covers every tool: tool.expose
A block of an unknown kind covers every tool: tool.result
A block of an unknown kind covers every model: model.invoke
A block of an unknown kind covers every model: model.result
A block of an unknown kind and a tool block both cover the call: the decision names either
A block of an unknown kind covers a tool that the catalog does not list: catalog.blocked, not catalog.unknown
A tool of a listed server that the catalog does not list
A listed tool's name on another server: tools resolve by their reference, never by their name alone
One of the agent's own tools that the catalog does not list
A built-in tool that the catalog does not list
A listed built-in tool's type of another provider
A listed model's name on another endpoint
A server whose URL url_host cannot read makes no reference: catalog.unknown without a SHA-256, and the server block of the host that a parser would read covers nothing
A model whose endpoint url_host cannot read makes no reference: catalog.unknown without a SHA-256
A provider block covers a model whose endpoint makes no reference, by its provider
What a reference leaves out, user information, query, fragment, case and the default port, resolves to the listed server
A URL with a secret path segment resolves, once redacted with the deployment's rules, to the listed server
A server block covers the server by its redacted reference
A local server resolves by its command line
The same local server launched with another root is another server
A bundle without a catalog file reads as an empty catalog: a tool is catalog.unknown
A bundle without a catalog file: a model is catalog.unknown
A bundle without a catalog file: blocks still cover
A discovered tool, also not enabled: row 3 comes first
A discovered model
An approved tool that is not enabled for the agent
An approved model that is not enabled for the agent
A tool that is not enabled, whose definition also changed: row 4 comes first
A tool whose definition differs from the pinned one
A tool whose definition, as the agent has it now, has no hash
A built-in tool has no definition: row 5 does not apply
A model whose runtime digest differs from the pinned one
A model with a pinned digest, whose runtime reports none
A model whose runtime digest is the pinned one
A model without a pinned digest passes whatever digest its runtime reports
The result of a tool that is not enabled passes the catalog check, and policies decide
The result of a discovered tool passes the catalog check
The result of a tool whose definition changed passes the catalog check
The result of a tool that the catalog does not list has no properties: error.invalid_request
A block keeps a tool's result from the agent
The result of a model whose digest differs passes the catalog check
The result of a model that is not enabled passes the catalog check
The result of a model that the catalog does not list has no properties: error.invalid_request
A block keeps a model's result from the agent
The gate comes before the catalog check
error.unknown_agent comes before the catalog check
A block comes before the arguments: an address that email_domain cannot read
catalog.unknown comes before the arguments: arguments that are not an object
catalog.not_enabled comes before the arguments
An enabled tool whose argument does not fit its declaration: error.invalid_request (EP-19)
An enabled tool whose arguments repeat a member name: error.invalid_request (EP-19)
Then policies: a policy reads the record that EP-19 filled, the transform applied, and forbids
Then policies: the same policy does not apply to another domain, and wt-catalog permits
Then policies: without wt-catalog, no policy permits an enabled tool
